clusters.headline: How OpenAI Used Its Own LLMs to Design Its Jalapeño Chip

items.title: How OpenAI Used Its Own LLMs to Design Its Jalapeño Chip
items.extract: On 25 August, OpenAI fully unveiled Jalapeño, the company’s debut AI accelerator chip. Jalapeño delivers up to 13.4 petaflops of 4-bit compute and accesses 232 gigabytes of the most advanced memory available, linking to it at a blazing 15.4 terabytes per second. Benchmarks cited by OpenAI show that Jalapeño can reduce end-to-end latency (the time between prompt to last token) by up to 3.6 times when compared to Nvidia’s GB300 —a chip the company currently relies on—and do so while consuming less power. Whether these figures translate into real-world gains once Jalapeño enters widespread service in OpenAI’s inference fleet remains to be seen, but performance is only half the story.

clusters.headline: Embedding Prediction Helps Image Generation

items.title: Embedding Prediction Helps Image Generation
items.extract: In diffusion transformers, a class label or a text prompt is embedded once, and the same condition is reused at every denoising step. We ask whether predicted embeddings can serve as this condition instead. Next-Embedding Predictive Autoregression (NEPA) trains a Transformer to predict the next continuous embedding in a sequence. In generation, the clean image follows the noisy image, so its embeddings are the next embeddings after the condition and the noisy image.

items.title: How Diffusion Controller unifies and simplifies AI image generation

clusters.summary: Embedding prediction improves image generation by utilizing predicted embeddings instead of reusing a single class label or text prompt condition across every denoising step in diffusion transformers. A new method called Next-Embedding Predictive Autoregression (NEPA) trains a Transformer to forecast the next continuous embedding within a sequence. During generation, the clean image follows the noisy image, making its embeddings the subsequent embeddings that follow both the condition and the noisy image.

clusters.headline: Finetuning with Sampling: SFT Learns Better Than You Think

items.title: Finetuning with Sampling: SFT Learns Better Than You Think
items.extract: Introducing new capabilities to frontier models has long been the goal of posttraining, which predominantly employs supervised finetuning (SFT) and reinforcement learning (RL) to this end. Conventional wisdom dictates that RL enables strong generalization on new tasks without losing existing capabilities, while SFT is prone to weak generalization and catastrophic forgetting. At the same time, SFT can learn from off-policy expert data, whereas RL must rely on a model's ability to find successful trajectories with repeated sampling. In our work, we seek to leverage the strength of on-policy learning while utilizing the privileged information contained in off-policy data.

clusters.summary: Finetuning with Sampling proves that SFT learns better than conventional wisdom dictates. Standard posttraining relies heavily on supervised finetuning and reinforcement learning to introduce new capabilities to frontier models. Traditional beliefs hold that RL provides strong generalization on new tasks while avoiding capability loss, whereas SFT suffers from weak generalization and catastrophic forgetting. Additionally, SFT utilizes off-policy expert data, while RL depends on a model finding successful trajectories through repeated sampling. New research aims to combine the advantages of on-policy learning with the privileged information found in off-policy data.

clusters.headline: TACO: Ternary Absolute-max Column-wise One-sparse Optimizer for LLM Fine-Tuning

items.title: TACO: Ternary Absolute-max Column-wise One-sparse Optimizer for LLM Fine-Tuning
items.extract: Full-parameter fine-tuning of large language models (LLMs) incurs substantial optimizer state memory overhead, limiting the model sizes that fit on modern GPUs. Existing approaches either compress optimizer state, abandon first-order gradients, or change the update geometry while retaining dense state. The recently introduced Muon optimizer reduces optimizer memory through matrix-valued updates. Still, its geometry differs from AdamW and can lead to performance degradation when fine-tuning AdamW-pretrained models.

clusters.summary: The newly introduced TACO (Ternary Absolute-max Column-wise One-sparse Optimizer) addresses the heavy optimizer state memory overhead that full-parameter fine-tuning of large language models (LLMs) places on modern GPUs, which otherwise restricts model sizes. Current methods attempt to solve this by compressing optimizer states, discarding first-order gradients, or altering update geometry while maintaining a dense state. Meanwhile, the recently introduced Muon optimizer lowers optimizer memory via matrix-valued updates, though its geometry diverges from AdamW and can cause performance drops when fine-tuning models pretrained with AdamW.

items.title: Decoding Looped Transformers Better for (Almost) Free
items.extract: Looped Transformers achieve parameter efficiency by repeatedly executing a shared block across recurrent loops. Each loop yields an intermediate representation decodable for the same next token, yet standard decoding discards earlier states. Because earlier loops embody less computation, recurrence inherently supplies aligned weak-and-strong prediction pairs without auxiliary models or external training.

clusters.headline: AI beats licensed accountants on speed and accuracy, but still can't close the books without supervision

items.title: AI beats licensed accountants on speed and accuracy, but still can't close the books without supervision
items.extract: According to a Mercor study, current AI models now outperform licensed CPAs on structured accounting tasks in both speed and accuracy. Eighteen months ago, they still lagged far behind. On the more demanding APEX Benchmark, though, no model fully completes all the tasks. Without human oversight, AI still can't close the books on its own.

clusters.summary: Current artificial intelligence models outperform licensed certified public accountants on structured accounting tasks in both speed and accuracy, according to a study by Mercor. Eighteen months ago, these systems still lagged far behind humans. However, on the more demanding APEX Benchmark, no model is able to fully complete all tasks. Consequently, artificial intelligence still cannot close the books independently without human oversight.

items.title: Apple says it’s tightening macOS ‘Full Disk Access’ controls due to new risks from AI agents
items.extract: Apple says it will add new controls around macOS’s Full Disk Access permission, warning that increasingly capable AI agents make broad access to users’ files, messages, mail, and browsing history riskier.

clusters.summary: Apple announced it will introduce new security controls for the macOS Full Disk Access permission. The company stated that the growing sophistication of AI agents increases the dangers associated with granting broad access to a user's browsing history, mail, messages, and files.

clusters.summary: President Donald Trump convened major tech CEOs—including Mark Zuckerberg, Jeff Bezos, Elon Musk, and Anthropic's Dario Amodei—at the White House this week to sign a "morally binding" AI safety pledge, while consumer adoption of AI and super intelligence sits at just 2%.
